interest: This document is historically interesting as evidence of wartime alert and rumors regarding Japanese naval activity along the Pacific coast of the Americas immediately following the outbreak of the Pacific War. It illustrates the State Department's monitoring of press reports and intelligence regarding suspected Imperial Japanese Navy submarine operations near strategic Mexican ports like Mazatlán, reflecting joint U.S.-Mexican hemispheric defense concerns in early 1942. Additionally, the docket sheet provides insight into State Department record-keeping practices and classification under decimal file 894.3312.
overview: This file (894.3312, File 191) consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloging records under the subject 'Visits of Japanese War Vessels to Mexico' (specifically visits of vessels and aircraft of Japan to ports of Mexico). The sheet indexes sub-number 26, a despatch (No. 15208) sent from Mexico by U.S. diplomat Raleigh A. Gibson on January 30, 1942. The indexed despatch transmitted Mexican news clippings and English translations concerning the reported presence of an Imperial Japanese Navy submarine operating off the coast near Mazatlán during the opening months of World War II in the Pacific.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers docket sheet indexing a January 1942 diplomatic despatch from Mexico regarding rumors of a Japanese submarine off Mazatlán.
subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State 'List of Papers' inventory sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, for decimal file 894.3312 concerning visits of Japanese war vessels to Mexico. It lists sub-file 26, a despatch (No. 15208) forwarded from Mexico by Raleigh A. Gibson on January 30, 1942. The entry records the transmission of Mexican news items and translations regarding the suspected presence of a Japanese submarine near the port of Mazatlán shortly after the United States entered World War II.
